title: Enslaved to Sense, to Pleasure Prone
description: Enslaved to Sense, to Pleasure Prone in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: John Wesley printed these words in A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780), hymn 108. They first appeared in a book he and his brother Charles published together, and the Collection's own index cannot say which of the two wrote them.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Common Metre (8.6.8.6), and this page sets them to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: En-slaved to sense, to plea-sure prone, Fond of cre-a-ted good, Fa-ther, our help-less-ness we own, And trem-bling taste our food.

lines: Enslaved to sense, to pleasure prone,
Fond of created good,
Father, our helplessness we own,
And trembling taste our food.
Trembling we taste; for, ah! no more
To thee the creatures lead;
Changed, they exert a baneful power,
And poison while they feed.
Cursed for the sake of wretched man,
They now engross him whole;
With pleasing force on earth detain,
And sensualize his soul.
Grovelling on earth we still must lie,
Till Christ the curse repeal;
Till Christ, descending from on high,
Infected nature heal.
Come then, our heavenly Adam, come,
Thy healing influence give,
Hallow our food, reverse our doom,
And bid us eat and live!
The bondage of corruption break,
For this our spirits groan;
Thy only will we fain would seek,
O save us from our own!
Turn the full stream of nature's tide;
Let all our actions tend
To thee their source; thy love the guide,
Thy glory be the end.
Earth then a scale to heaven shall be,
Sense shall point out the road,
The creatures all shall lead to thee,
And all we taste be God.

source: John Wesley, A Collection of Hymns for the Use of the People Called Methodists (1780)
licence: Public domain: Charles Wesley died in 1788; John Wesley died in 1791.
credits: Words by Charles Wesley (1707–1788) or John Wesley (1703–1791), public domain, as printed in John Wesley's Collection of Hymns (1780); set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
